item.title: Hermes AI Agent Targets Thai Finance Ministry; OnTrac Discloses Customer Data Breach
item.content:encoded:
Hermes AI agent used to automate attack on Thai Finance Ministry — Should Read

Attackers reportedly used the open-source Hermes AI agent in unattended “YOLO” mode to automate post-exploitation activity against Thailand’s Ministry of Finance, including privilege-escalation checks, service enumeration, and file system searches. Exposed attacker directories revealed tools, logs, credentials, web shells, and implants, though the ministry has not confirmed a breach.

  • Hunt.io and researcher Bob Diachenko found exposed web directories containing hundreds of files tied to an alleged operation against Thailand’s Ministry of Finance.
  • The exposed files included exploit code, web shells, HTTP tunneling tools, custom scripts, stolen credentials, compiled payloads, and Hermes AI agent logs.
  • Recovered Hermes logs showed the operator enabled YOLO mode, allowing the AI agent to run commands without human approval at each step.
  • The Hermes agent was used for post-exploitation tasks including privilege-escalation checks, kernel vulnerability scanning, service enumeration, SUID and SGID binary searches, container inspection, and file system traversal.
  • Thailand’s Ministry of Finance has not confirmed a breach, and Hunt.io said some artifacts only showed that systems were targeted rather than successfully compromised.

OnTrac notifies customers of data breach after network hack — Should Read

OnTrac says hackers breached its corporate network in March and may have accessed customer personal information, though it has not disclosed exactly what data or how many people were affected. The company is offering 12 months of credit monitoring and says it has no evidence the stolen information has been published or misused.

  • OnTrac says hackers breached its corporate network and may have accessed personal details belonging to its customers.
  • The incident was detected on March 23, and OnTrac’s investigation found that the attacker accessed certain files between March 20 and March 22.
  • Apart from names, the types of exposed information are unclear because OnTrac redacted the data elements in the notification sample shared with authorities.
  • OnTrac is offering affected customers 12 months of free credit monitoring and identity protection through CyberScout, with a 90-day enrollment deadline.
  • At the time of publication, no ransomware or data extortion group had claimed responsibility for the attack.

Ground Truth for Every Security Function — Optional

Censys argues that modern security teams need a live, first-party map of Internet infrastructure to make faster decisions across triage, investigation, threat hunting, and defense. The article positions Censys Internet Map, Platform, ARC, and related signals as the shared “ground truth” layer for those workflows.

  • Censys built the Censys Internet Map as a first-party view of hosts, services, certificates, DNS, web properties, software, protocols, exposures, and infrastructure changes on the Internet.
  • Censys Platform is intended to let practitioners search, enrich, pivot, automate, monitor, and act on Internet Map data within their existing tools and workflows.
  • Censys ARC adds expert judgment to raw Internet observations, such as identifying commodity hosting, adversary-like infrastructure, risky service exposure, and urgent findings.
  • The article says SOC analysts, incident responders, threat hunters, detection engineers, network defenders, and vulnerability teams use Censys data across triage, investigation, hunting, and defense workflows.
  • Censys argues that triage, investigation, hunting, and defense are connected parts of modern security work that all depend on the same external Internet data.
